taxonomy.note: Current Kew/POWO accepts Vitis cinerea but excludes the Heller/berlandieri concept as the separate species Vitis berlandieri. Flora of North America uses a broader V. cinerea concept with var. helleri included. This mismatch makes older Central Texas county records unsafe for direct transfer to current V. cinerea.

evidence: Kew/POWO accepts Vitis cinerea and recognizes Texas in the native range, but does not include var. helleri among its accepted infraspecifics.
Flora of North America states var. cinerea is found in Texas only in the eastern part of the state and intergrades with var. helleri southwest of the Brazos River.

USDA-derived species-level county data include Central Texas counties, but those records may aggregate the older helleri/berlandieri concept and are therefore not used to satisfy the three-county rule.
target_zone_range.blocking_issue: Fewer than three exact target-zone counties are verified under the current taxon concept.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Do not count Central Texas species-level Vitis cinerea records until they are reconciled against the current Kew concept and separated from V. berlandieri.

morphology.look_here_first: Treat this as a concept-check species. In the strict var. cinerea morphology, branchlets are distinctly angled and densely short-hairy plus cobwebby; leaf undersides stay visibly gray/green with both webby and short hairs, and berries are small and only slightly glaucous. Do not call a Central Texas Heller's grape V. cinerea solely because an app uses a broad species concept.
diagnostic_traits: strict var. cinerea branchlets densely hirtellous and arachnoid
leaves cordate, usually unlobed to shallowly 3-shouldered
lower leaf surface visible through sparse-to-moderate webby/short hairs
berries black, 4–8 mm, slightly or not glaucous
strict var. cinerea favors floodplains, lowland woods and stream margins and is primarily eastern in Texas

confusers.separator: The Central Texas Heller/berlandieri concept has much sparser lower-surface hair, strongly glaucous fruit and Edwards Plateau limestone affinity; current Kew treats it as a separate species.
Mustang grape has a dense opaque white-felted leaf underside and much larger berries.
V. palmata has uniformly red branchlets and deeply lobed glabrous leaves.

diagnostic_roles: lower leaf surface showing webby plus short hairs

installation_guardrail: Do not install as a project-native taxon until three exact target-zone counties are verified under the current taxonomic concept.
